`testRejectedDrainLoggingDoesNotHoldOutboxMonitor` timed out in host stop in the required full-suite check holding https://github.com/CodexCoder21Organization/UrlProtocol/pull/635. The first failure is recorded at https://github.com/CodexCoder21Organization/UrlProtocol/actions/runs/40085745929/job/120848195951; the owner requested local reproduction and a fix at its source, without CI reruns or publication.

A completed connection-close promise could lose its conversion callback when its live event-loop queue was full. Netty logs “Event loop shut down?” for that rejection too. The Java future then remained pending after the queue recovered. Both conversion overloads now copy terminal results directly and recheck completion after registering a pending operation's listener.

Six deterministic public-API cases failed before the change and when only the converter was reversed. They cover channel and generic futures, full live and terminated executors, exact success/failure/cancellation, and completion at listener registration. The initial fixed local run passed 23/23 tests including close ownership, explicit retries, shutdown timing and AsyncExt neighbors. Full records and reproduction source are preserved on https://github.com/CodexCoder21Organization/jvm-libp2p/tree/wip/FL635-20261024 and https://github.com/CodexCoder21Organization/UrlProtocol/tree/wip/FL635-20261024.

The downstream deterministic loopback host test failed 3/3 with the same stack against snapshot-25 and passed against this locally built library. Main and the exact PR head both reproduced the original cleanup timeout with the same 128-cycle, eight-worker amplifier. A separate fixture cleanup proposal awaits owner approval; it addresses a close command legitimately rejected while that test's injected queue work is still pending.

This prepares `community.kotlin.libp2p:jvm-libp2p:1.3.0-codexcoder21-snapshot-41`. Nothing was published or deployed. Only local checks were run; no CI check was rerun, requested, or watched.
